data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic spirituality, Nisrin represents the embodiment of divine love and beauty. It symbolizes the inner beauty and radiance that comes from a deep connection with the divine, and can serve as a reminder to cultivate inner virtues and spiritual growth. Theological scholars argue that the prophet Moses' wife, Sephora or Zipporah, was called Nisrin in the Quran and that the word 'Nisrin' represents the celestial Venus which is associated with love, mercy, grace and abundance in nature. The name Nisrin is thus a symbol of the divine feminine and can inspire a sense of reverence and awe for the manifestations of divine love and beauty in the world.
